title: Which number do these tokens make?
description: Farhan sorts paper tokens at a school mela in Hyderabad. The video counts each kind into the chart, writes the number and says its name.
teaching_notes: One idea: count each kind of token into its column, then count three places from the right for the comma. Watch for the comma placed from the left.

source: Tokens: one 10,000, one 1,000, two 100, one 10, four 1. Writ
video_script.why: The child can add a few small tokens to ten thousand but has not yet used tokens of every size.
video_script.substitution: Count each kind of token into its column, add the values, place the comma three places from the right and say the name.
video_script.anchor: Farhan's paper tokens at his school mela in Hyderabad
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu puts the comma after three digits from the left. The comma sits three places from the right, after the thousands place.
video_script.payoff_line: that makes eleven thousand two hundred fourteen
maths_rules: tokens: one 10,000, one 1,000, two 100, one 10, four 1
chart: TTh 1, Th 1, H 2, T 1, O 4
comma after the Th place, three places from the right: 11,214
name: eleven thousand two hundred fourteen (the thousands part is eleven)
slip: digits 11214 with the comma after three digits from the left gives 112,14, which is wrong
your turn: one 10,000, three 1,000, five 100, no 10 tokens and six 1 tokens; 10,000 + 3,000 + 500 + 0 + 6 = 13,506; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: count each kind of token into its column, add, comma, name. Wrong idea: the comma counted from the left. The token stall stays as the anchor; the chart builds on the stage.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a table at a school mela with a tray of paper tokens sorted in five heaps: one 10,000 token, one 1,000 token, two 100 tokens, one 10 token and four 1 tokens; an empty chart with columns TTh, Th, H, T and O

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.sort: the tray of sorted token heaps appears
marks.heaps: each heap lights up in turn
marks.ask: an empty chart appears beside the tray

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='sort'/>Farhan sorts paper tokens at his school mela in Hyderabad.
<bookmark mark='heaps'/>He has one ten thousand token and one thousand token. He also has two hundred tokens, one ten token and four one tokens.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which number do these tokens make, and what is its name?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the heaps slide into the chart, one heap to each column; a count label sits over each column

marks.slide: each heap slides into its own column
marks.count: a count label appears over each column

narration: <bookmark mark='slide'/>Put each kind of token in its own column of the chart.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Then count how many tokens each column holds.
<bookmark mark='empty'/>If a column has no tokens, we write a zero there to hold the place.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows the five digits in a row with a comma after the third digit from the left; arrows count three places from the right; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with a comma after three digits from the left
marks.right: arrows count three places from the right
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>I write the digits in a row and count three from the left. That gives one hundred twelve comma fourteen.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Count three places from the right instead, ones, tens and hundreds.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The comma goes after those three places, counted from the right.

beats.on_screen: the chart reads TTh 1, Th 1, H 2, T 1, O 4; the board shows 10,000 + 1,000 + 200 + 10 + 4 = 11,214

marks.num: the number 11,214 appears with its comma

narration: <bookmark mark='chart'/>The chart has one, one, two, one and four, from the left.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add the values, ten thousand, one thousand, two hundred, ten and four.
<bookmark mark='num'/>That makes eleven thousand two hundred fourteen, with the comma after the thousands.

beats.on_screen: the number 11,214 splits at the comma into 11 and 214; the name card appears under it
narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Read the part before the comma first. It is eleven, and then we say thousand.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Then read the last three digits, which are two hundred fourteen.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Say the name aloud, and check it against the digits in the chart.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the token table; two lines appear: count each kind into its column; comma three places from the right; then a new set of tokens with an empty chart

marks.one: the line count each kind into its column appears
marks.two: the line comma three places from the right appears
marks.turn: a new set of tokens and an empty chart appear

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Count each kind of token into its own column.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Put the comma three places from the right.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Your turn. One ten thousand token, three thousand tokens, five hundred tokens and six one tokens. Write the number and its name.
